learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of solving degree-2 polynomial equations using factorization and the magical Quadratic Formula, and understand the nature of their roots!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A quadratic equation in the variable x is an equation of the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a ≠ 0.
Also known as 'splitting the middle term'. You split the middle term 'bx' into two terms whose sum is 'b' and whose product is 'a × c', then factor by grouping.
If factorization is too hard, use the universal formula! The roots are given by x = [-b ± √(b^2 - 4ac)] / 2a.
The value inside the square root, D = b^2 - 4ac, is called the discriminant. It determines the 'nature' of the roots without actually solving the equation.
If D > 0, there are two distinct real roots. If D = 0, there are two equal real roots. If D < 0, there are no real roots (the graph doesn't touch the x-axis).

fun_activity.title: 🚀 The Rocket Launch
fun_activity.instructions: When a rocket is launched, its height over time forms a quadratic equation! If the height equation is h = -5t^2 + 20t, find the time (t) when the height is 0 (hits the ground). Just solve -5t^2 + 20t = 0!

exam_tips: 📌 When finding the roots using the quadratic formula, always calculate the Discriminant (D = b^2 - 4ac) first to avoid calculation errors.
📌 Pay special attention to word problems involving the speed of a train or a motorboat going upstream/downstream.
📌 If a question states 'the roots are equal', immediately set D = 0 (b^2 - 4ac = 0) to find the unknown variable 'k'.
quick_recap: ⭐ The 'roots' of a quadratic equation are the exact same thing as the 'zeroes' of a quadratic polynomial.
⭐ A quadratic equation MUST have an x^2 term. If a = 0, it becomes a linear equation.
⭐ The quadratic formula was mathematically derived using the method of completing the square.
